subject: Throughput carveout and queueing policy for Reserved Capacity - EurEnergia
messages:
From: Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@eurenergia.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Novak <elena.novak@eurenergia.com>, procurement@eurenergia.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 08:17:00 +0100
Subject: Dedicated pool: throughput carveout request and queueing behavior

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our SRE team reviewed the Dedicated pool behavior and we'd like to propose a carveout in the throughput SLA for our energy forecasting workload. During peak billing windows we need guaranteed tail throughput for high-priority model runs (latency target: p95 < 120ms).

Key asks:
- A small steady carveout of 6 reserved GPUs (from our 48-GPU pool) to be given priority scheduling for jobs tagged "billing-critical".
- Queueing behavior for these jobs: no more than 300ms queueing before preemption of lower-priority work.
- Fallback plan: if the pool cannot meet the carveout, automatic fallback to a compatible model variant with documented degradation and a 5% credit per missed SLO.

We are starting procurement discussions but need a technical confirmation of whether Redwood can support the carveout behavior and the preemption window. I've attached our internal runbook excerpt for context.

Regards,
Marco
Head of Platform Engineering
EurEnergia

Attachment: eurenergia-runbook-excerpt.pdf (attachment stub)
From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@eurenergia.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 09:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: throughput carveout request and queueing behavior

Hi Marco — thanks for the clear ask and the runbook. Quick answers up front: yes, we can implement a carveout-style priority slice for your reserved pool; the details and limits depend on autoscaling and the existing burst policy.

I've attached an initial SLO appendix that maps carveout semantics to our queueing primitives (priority classes, preemptible slots, and fallback variants). A few immediate points:
- We can reserve dedicated GPU slots tagged for your billing-critical class. Those slots will be excluded from standard burst allocation but participate in autoscale when pool utilization is high.
- Preemption window: we can guarantee a maximum queueing latency of 300ms for your tagged jobs under normal operating conditions; under severe contention (region-level capacity pressure) we fall back to the compatible variant and trigger the fallback credit policy.
- Crediting: the contract language needs to define the measurement window (we propose a 1-hour rolling window for credits).

Next steps: Aditya, can you confirm on the telemetry side whether we can export the p95 measurement and the preemption metrics to EurEnergia's SIEM? Also, Laura, procurement and legal will need a clause for the fallback crediting.

Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA-carveout-appendix-v2.pdf (attachment stub)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 11:48:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: throughput carveout request and queueing behavior

Camila — technical note from infra:

We support priority classes and can tag reserved GPUs at allocation time. Implementation detail and risk:
- The preemption mechanism uses a two-tier token bucket; under steady state it's reliable for sub-300ms queueing. However, if there is simultaneous regional surge affecting multiple customers and cross-tenant bursting is in effect, the hard bound can't be guaranteed unless EurEnergia accepts a carveout that reduces burst capacity by ~8% during trading hours.
- We'll need to add a named metric (eurenergia.billing_critical.preemptions) and emit it to your SIEM (we can push via the existing streaming hook).
- Queueing-diagram attached to clarify the scheduling flow.

If procurement is looking to avoid reducing burst headroom, the alternative is a soft-priority plus negotiated financial credit when the hard bound isn't achievable.

—Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer

Attachment: queueing-diagram-v1.png (attachment stub)
From: Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@eurenergia.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Novak <elena.novak@eurenergia.com>, procurement@eurenergia.com
Date: Fri, 23 Jan 2026 14:10:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: throughput carveout request and queueing behavior

Camila, Aditya — thanks for the fast turnaround. A couple clarifications from our side:

1) We understand the headroom tradeoff. Our preference is to preserve burst capacity during most hours but lock hard guarantees during our 4-hour daily settlement window (03:00–07:00 CET). Can we express the carveout as time-bound (enforced only during settlement windows)?

2) Credits: the 1-hour rolling window is fine; procurement will likely ask for an explicit SLA table that lists credits per missed p95 measurement per hour.

3) Telemetry: yes, please add eurenergia.billing_critical.preemptions to the stream. We also want a lightweight dashboard in Redwood Console for the settlement window.

If it's easier, we can approve a temporary mitigation (soft priority plus 10% credits) while your infra team implements the hard carveout enforcement. We'd like to close this by end of next week to align with our procurement timeline.

Marco

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: throughput carveout request and queueing behavior

Hi Marco — summary and proposed path forward:

1) Time-bound carveout: Redwood will implement a settlement-window carveout (03:00–07:00 CET) that pins 6 GPUs for the "billing-critical" priority class. Outside the window those GPUs will contribute to burst headroom.
2) Preemption guarantee: We will aim to guarantee p95 queueing < 300ms during the window. As Aditya noted, this is contingent on region-level capacity; if region-wide capacity pressure occurs we will:
   - Trigger an automatic fallback to the compatible model variant;
   - Emit a miss event and calculate a credit per agreed SLA table (we propose starting draft values in the attached appendix).
3) Telemetry & dashboard: Infra will emit eurenergia.billing_critical.preemptions to your SIEM and we will enable a Redwood Console dashboard scoped to the settlement window.
4) Temporary path: If you need immediate contractual language for procurement we can sign a temporary amendment that provides soft-priority with a 10% credits floor while we complete the enforcement work (estimated 10 business days).

Action items:
- Procurement: please confirm whether the temporary amendment is acceptable (procurement@eurenergia.com).
- Aditya: please confirm the final export hook name and ETA for the dashboard.
- Laura/legal: please prepare a 1-page amendment and the SLA table for credits.

If we can get procurement sign-off by end of week, we'll open an infra ticket and aim for enforcement test in 10 business days.

Thanks all — Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
